why: The whole reason `.ui-btn` has size MODIFIERS rather than a size: the pause panel's Mute and the three toggles beside it are a smaller control than the slab a panel stacks, and flattening the two into one size is the tidy-looking edit that erases the distinction. Every button still looks themed under this mutation -- `.ui-btn` supplies fill, text colour and cursor either way -- so `never lets a button fall through to browser default styling` stays green and only `keeps each size of quiet control to ONE size` notices, because that case measures each size group against the OTHER group as well as against itself. Without its final `not.toBe`, the two loops would both pass on a stylesheet that gave every button in the HUD one shape.
killedBy: hud.css is syntactically whole keeps each size of quiet control to ONE size, which is what the modifier is for
